content.comment_body: I'm using [product_name] with [product_name] and reading two temperature values. My plan was to control a water pump on a heat exchanger by setting the temperature difference as a reference variable for the built-in PI controller. Unfortunately, I haven't found a block element that can calculate the difference between two analog signals. Is there a way or workaround to achieve this calculation?
Have you considered using the analog comparator?

The analog comparator I checked only gives a binary output. Since my goal is to get the temperature difference and use it as feedback for the controller via the PV input, I need an analog signal. Is there any method to obtain an analog output from the analog comparator? Any suggestions would be appreciated. Thanks.
If you have a [article_no] version of [product_name], it's possible. You can use the analog MUX and the reference function, as shown in the example program I attached. Does this help you?

Good morning [user_name], that was exactly the issue I faced, and your solution worked. Thank you. Your example could be useful as part of the example programs found on the [company_name] product pages. Have a great day.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are frustrated by the lack of an easy method to calculate the difference between two analog signals using available blocks in [product_name] with [product_name]. They want to process analog signals directly, but the current block elements, especially analog comparators, only provide binary outputs. The solution using analog MUX and reference function was effective but not immediately apparent, showing that analog processing features could be more intuitive in [product_name].
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to directly calculate the difference between two analog signals and use this value as an analog input for control functions within [product_name].
